issues.display_title: Issue #52: Ranking freshness: decide penalty mechanism (query-time vs generated column vs cron)
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #52 — Ranking Freshness: Penalty Mechanism Decision

Status: Done (decision recorded, implementation shipped in PR #60)
Type: Architecture decision, no code change of its own
Depends on: none — blocks #53, #54, #56, #57, #58

Problem

ranking is a stored column on DirectoryPhotographer (src/models/directory_photographer.go:27), written only by RecomputeAndSaveRanking (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go), which fires from 16 write paths. A profile untouched for over a year performs no writes, so RecomputeAndSaveRanking never fires for it — putting a freshness penalty inside ComputeRanking itself would be dead code for exactly the profiles it's meant to penalize.

Decision

Option A — query-time SQL expression. The v2 search orders by a penalized expression instead of the raw ranking column:

ORDER BY GREATEST(ranking - CASE WHEN (updated_at IS NULL OR updated_at < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 365 DAY)) THEN 20 ELSE 0 END, 0) DESC
  • The ranking column keeps its current meaning: the base score (tierBaseline + fieldBonus). It is written exactly as before.
  • The penalty is never persisted — it's derived at read time, so it self-heals the moment any write bumps updated_at.
  • No migration, no schema change, no cron job. The repo has no migration mechanism at all, so this also avoids introducing one.

Rejected alternatives

  • Option B (persisted effective_ranking column + daily job): MySQL forbids non-deterministic functions (NOW()) in generated columns, for both VIRTUAL and STORED. This collapses into Option C plus an extra column — not a distinct mechanism.
  • Option C (bake penalty into ComputeRanking + daily BackfillRanking cron): Destroys the base score — once penalty is baked into ranking, a decayed Agency profile can no longer be distinguished from a fresh Pro one, and restoring a score requires a recompute instead of it happening automatically. Also introduces up to 24h staleness and a new cron dependency.

On query cost

ranking has no index today (no index gorm tags on DirectoryPhotographer, only unique constraints on gothru_user_id/slug/email), so the existing ORDER BY ranking DESC, rating_avg DESC, id DESC is already an unindexed filesort. Option A introduces no ordering regression versus the pre-existing baseline. Indexability was tracked separately in #56.

Outcome

Implemented in PR #60 (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go). See issue-54-v2-search-ordering-implementation.md for the implementation detail.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17

Blocks every other task in this breakdown. Pick the mechanism before writing code.

Problem

ranking is a stored column (src/models/directory_photographer.go:27), written only by RecomputeAndSaveRanking (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go:103), which fires from 16 write paths.

A profile that has not been updated in over a year performs no writes — so RecomputeAndSaveRanking never fires for it. Putting the freshness penalty inside ComputeRanking therefore makes it dead code for exactly the profiles it is meant to penalise. The score would only decay for profiles that are actively being edited, which is backwards.

Options

A. Query-time SQL expression (recommended)

Order the v2 search by the penalised score instead of the raw column:

ORDER BY (ranking - CASE WHEN updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL 1 YEAR THEN <penalty> ELSE 0 END) DESC

The ranking column keeps its current meaning and is still written exactly as today — it holds the base score (tierBaseline + fieldBonus, 0-79). The penalty is never persisted; it is derived at read time.

  • Self-healing: the penalty appears and disappears purely as a function of the clock, no job required.
  • Satisfies AC3 for free — any write that bumps updated_at immediately restores the full score on the next query.
  • No migration, no schema change, no new infrastructure.
  • Cost: the v2 keyset-pagination cursor must compare the same expression (see #54).

B. New persisted column effective_ranking + scheduled job

Correction: an earlier version of this issue proposed a generated column. That is not possible. MySQL forbids non-deterministic functions (NOW(), CURRENT_DATE) in generated column expressions — for both VIRTUAL and STORED, not just STORED. A freshness penalty cannot be expressed as a generated column at all.

So this option is really: a plain column, filled by a daily job that walks the table and recomputes base - penalty.

  • Indexable, so ORDER BY and the keyset WHERE can both use an index.
  • Cost: a migration, a cron job to own and monitor, a full-table write sweep every day, and up to 24h of staleness at the boundary.
  • This collapses into option C plus an extra column — it is not a separate mechanism.

C. Penalty inside ComputeRanking + daily cron calling BackfillRanking

Smallest code diff — the existing BackfillRanking endpoint already walks every photographer (src/action/v1/photographers/maintenance.go:105).

  • Cost: up to 24h staleness, a full-table sweep daily, new cron infrastructure.
  • Worse: the base score is destroyed. Once penalty is baked into ranking, you can no longer distinguish a decayed Agency from a fresh Pro, and restoring a score requires a recompute rather than just happening.
  • Also collides with #55 — see that issue.

Recommendation

Option A. No migration, no scheduled job, base score preserved, and AC3 falls out automatically. The only real work is threading the expression through the keyset cursor (#54).

On the "won't a CASE in ORDER BY be slow?" objection

ranking has no index today. There are no index gorm tags on DirectoryPhotographer and no migration files in the repo — only unique constraints on gothru_user_id, slug and email. So the current ORDER BY ranking DESC, rating_avg DESC, id DESC already performs a filesort.

Option A therefore introduces no ordering regression. And if index-backed ordering is wanted, a composite index on (ranking, rating_avg, id) can be added independently — it is orthogonal to the penalty mechanism.

Latency on this query is dominated by other things entirely (dead cross-DB fetch, cross-DB IN lists, three Preloads). Measured in #56.

Done when

  • Mechanism chosen and recorded in a comment on this issue.
  • If not Option A, the dependent tasks in this breakdown are re-scoped accordingly.

issues.display_title: Issue #53: Ranking freshness: product decision for stale-profile penalty
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #53 — Ranking Freshness: Penalty Magnitude and Curve Decision

Status: Done — product decision codified in the issue body, implementation matches exactly
Type: Product decision, no code change of its own
Depends on: #52 — blocks #54, #58

Problem

The acceptance criteria required a "ranking penalty / score decay" without specifying a number. ComputeRanking (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go) produces tierBaseline(subscription) + fieldBonus.

Real score range (corrected)

MaxFieldBonus = 19 exists but only 14 scorable items are reachable (9 profile fields + 5 collection flags), so the clamp never engages — it's dead code. The real, non-overlapping score bands are:

Tier Subscription values Range
Agency 5, 8 60–74
Pro 1, 6 40–54
Basic 2, 7 20–34
PAYG / Free anything else 0–14

Because the tier step (20) is larger than the max field bonus (14), there is a 5-point unreachable gap between every tier band (15–19, 35–39, 55–59) — tier always dominates profile completeness today.

Decision

  • Flat penalty, not graded: -20, applied once updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL 365 DAY (or updated_at IS NULL).
  • Formula: effective_ranking = max(base_ranking - 20, 0).
  • Boundary: <, not <=. Exactly 365 days old is still fresh.
  • NULL handling: treated as stale — no profile is exempt from freshness scoring by never having a recorded timestamp.
  • Floor: clamp at 0. Negative effective scores are unnecessary since ordering is the only consumer.
  • Intent — soft demotion, not a tier wipeout: a stale paid profile may still outrank a fresh lower-tier profile. At -20:
    • Any stale profile always ranks below every fresh profile of its own tier (band width 14–20 > penalty headroom within-tier).
    • A stale full Agency (74 − 20 = 54) ties a fresh full Pro (54) exactly — rating_avg then id break the tie. This is intentional, not an off-by-one: -20 sits just under the threshold (≥21) that would make a stale full Agency drop below every fresh Pro.
  • No time-scaling: a profile stale for 366 days and one stale for several years receive the identical -20 penalty. The penalty does not continue to grow.
  • Base column untouched: ranking remains the persisted base score; freshness is an ordering concern applied at query time, not a rewrite of the stored score.

Resolution history

This issue was originally opened with the "question" label pending product input. During implementation the decision was recorded twice as a comment (initial reasoning, then a correction after a review caught the MaxFieldBonus dead-code / real-range error). The issue body was subsequently rewritten by the product owner to codify the final decision directly — the codified body matches the implemented behavior exactly, verified line-by-line against src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go.

Outcome

Implemented in PR #60 as the freshnessPenalty = 20 / freshnessWindowDays = 365 constants in src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go, tested in getPhotographers_test.go (boundary, NULL, clamp cases). See issue-54-v2-search-ordering-implementation.md and issue-58-tests.md.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17
Depends on: #52

Product decision

Photographer ranking should use a flat freshness penalty when a profile has not been updated in over one year.

The freshness penalty is intended to be a soft demotion, not a full reset of ranking power. A stale paid profile may still outrank a fresh lower-tier profile if its subscription tier and profile completeness are strong enough.

Current base score model

ComputeRanking returns:

base ranking = tier baseline + field bonus

Tier baselines:

Tier Subscription values Baseline
Agency 5, 8 60
Pro 1, 6 40
Basic 2, 7 20
PAYG / Free anything else 0

Field bonus currently comes from 14 scorable items:

  • 9 profile fields
  • 5 collection flags

Although MaxFieldBonus = 19 exists, only 14 points are currently reachable. Therefore the real current score bands are:

Tier Fresh score range
Agency 60-74
Pro 40-54
Basic 20-34
PAYG / Free 0-14

Freshness penalty rule

Apply the following effective ranking rule at query time:

effective ranking = max(base ranking - freshness penalty, 0)

The freshness penalty is:

20 points

The penalty applies when:

updated_at IS NULL
OR updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL 365 DAY

Boundary behavior:

  • Exactly 365 days old is still considered fresh.
  • More than 365 days old is stale.
  • updated_at IS NULL is stale.
  • Effective ranking must never be negative.

Expected stale score bands

With a flat -20 penalty and a floor at 0:

Tier Fresh score range Stale effective score range
Agency 60-74 40-54
Pro 40-54 20-34
Basic 20-34 0-14
PAYG / Free 0-14 0

Product rationale

This penalty is intentionally meaningful but bounded:

  • A stale profile should rank below fresh profiles from the same tier.
  • Freshness should influence ranking, but should not completely erase subscription tier value.
  • The penalty should not continue increasing over time.
  • A profile stale for 366 days and a profile stale for multiple years receive the same -20 penalty.
  • The base ranking column should remain unchanged; freshness is an ordering concern, not a persisted score rewrite.

Implementation reference

Per #52, the chosen mechanism is query-time scoring. The stored ranking column remains the base score.

Implementation should apply the same effective ranking expression consistently in:

  • v2 search ordering
  • v2 keyset pagination cursor comparison
  • any response field decision documented by #54

Done when

  • #54 implements query-time effective ranking with the flat -20 freshness penalty.
  • #58 verifies stale, fresh, exact 365-day boundary, NULL updated_at, clamp-to-zero, reset behavior, and pagination stability.

issues.display_title: Issue #54: Ranking freshness: apply penalty to v2 search ordering and fix keyset cursor
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #54 — Apply Penalty to v2 Search Ordering and Fix Keyset Cursor

Status: Done — shipped in PR #60
Type: Implementation
Depends on: #52, #53

Scope

Apply the freshness penalty (#52 mechanism, #53 magnitude) to /v2/photographers/users search ordering, and keep keyset pagination correct across the penalty boundary. v1's getPhotographers.go (used only by the sitemap, per code inspection of every frontend fetcher) was explicitly out of scope and left untouched.

The core risk: keyset pagination

The existing cursor compared the raw ranking column in the WHERE clause while the intended ORDER BY would use a penalized expression. If the two diverge, pagination skips or duplicates rows across page boundaries — this was the primary implementation risk called out by the issue.

Implementation (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go)

A single SQL expression is shared between ORDER BY and the keyset WHERE, built from the same Go constants used for the in-memory computation, so the two cannot silently drift apart:

const freshnessPenalty = 20
const freshnessWindowDays = 365

var effectiveRankingExpr = fmt.Sprintf(
    "GREATEST(ranking - CASE WHEN (updated_at IS NULL OR updated_at < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL %d DAY)) THEN %d ELSE 0 END, 0)",
    freshnessWindowDays, freshnessPenalty,
)

func effectiveRanking(ranking int, updatedAt *time.Time, now time.Time) int {
    stale := updatedAt == nil || updatedAt.Before(now.AddDate(0, 0, -freshnessWindowDays))
    if stale {
        ranking -= freshnessPenalty
    }
    if ranking < 0 {
        ranking = 0
    }
    return ranking
}
  • ORDER BY: effectiveRankingExpr + " DESC", rating_avg DESC, id DESC — tiebreakers unchanged.
  • Keyset WHERE: the same effectiveRankingExpr string is substituted into the existing three-way OR comparison (rank / rank+rating / rank+rating+id), so the comparison and the ordering are provably the same expression.
  • Cursor row: its own effective score is computed in Go via effectiveRanking(cursorPhotographer.Ranking, cursorPhotographer.UpdatedAt, now) before being bound as a query parameter — not read as a raw column — so the cursor and the ordered rows are penalized consistently.
  • now is captured once per request and threaded through both the cursor computation and the per-row response mapping, so every row in a single response is judged against the same instant (and the boundary is deterministically testable — see #58).

API response field decision

Ranking in the JSON response (PhotographerResponse.Ranking) now returns the effective (penalized) score, not the raw stored column. Rationale: the response ordering already reflects the penalty; returning the raw column would show two profiles at the same number in a different order with no visible reason. This is a meaning change on a public field — documented in the PR description, and the stored ranking column itself is untouched.

Known accepted limitation (raised in PR review)

Cursor staleness is judged by the app clock (now, captured at request start); page rows are judged by NOW() in SQL (DB clock). A row sitting exactly at the 365-day boundary at request time can land on different sides of the two clocks, opening a seconds-wide skip/duplicate window. Accepted as-is (documented inline in the code) — narrow, and only affects rows crossing the boundary at that exact instant.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./... clean.
  • No changes to src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographers.go (sitemap path).
  • Pagination-across-boundary regression test — see issue-58-tests.md.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17
Depends on: #52, #53

This is the bulk of the work. Apply the freshness penalty to the v2 photographer search and keep pagination correct.

Why v2 only

Checked every frontend consumer in gothru-photographer-v2:

Fetcher Endpoint Used by
getPhotographers v1/photographers/users only src/app/sitemap.ts:18 — enumerates slugs for the sitemap, ordering irrelevant
getPhotographersV2 v2/photographers/users src/components/directory-page.tsx:166,189,228, src/app/page.tsx:86

Every user-facing ranked list goes through v2. v1 ordering is out of scope.

Before closing: confirm v1/photographers/users is not consumed by another client (admin panel, mobile). If it is, this task grows to cover src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographers.go:83.

The tricky part: keyset pagination

src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go:254-264 currently pages with a keyset cursor comparing the raw ranking column:

query = query.Where(
    "(ranking < ?) OR (ranking = ? AND (rating_avg < ? OR rating_avg IS NULL)) OR (ranking = ? AND rating_avg = ? AND id < ?)",
    cursorRanking,
    cursorRanking, cursorRating,
    cursorRanking, cursorRating, cursorPhotographer.ID,
)

...then orders by ranking DESC, rating_avg DESC, id DESC.

If the ORDER BY uses a penalised expression while the WHERE still compares raw ranking, pagination breaks — rows get skipped or duplicated across page boundaries. Both the cursor comparison and the ordering must use the same expression.

Note the cursor is derived from cursorPhotographer.Ranking (the stored value loaded from the cursor row), so the penalised value has to be computed for the cursor row too, not just for the rows being compared.

Scope

  • Apply the penalty expression to the ORDER BY in src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go:264.
  • Apply the identical expression to the keyset WHERE at lines 254-260.
  • Compute the cursor's penalised score consistently with the compared rows.
  • Keep the existing tiebreakers (rating_avg DESC, id DESC) intact.
  • Verify the Ranking int field exposed in the response (getPhotographers.go:35) — decide whether the API returns the raw or the penalised score, and keep it consistent.

Done when

  • v2 search ranks profiles stale for >365 days below equivalent fresh profiles.
  • Paging through the full result set returns each photographer exactly once, including across the penalty boundary.
  • No change to the v1 sitemap path.

issues.display_title: Issue #55: Ranking freshness: bump photographers.updated_at on child-table writes (AC3)
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #55 — Bump photographers.updated_at on Child-Table Writes (AC3)

Status: Done — shipped in PR #60
Type: Bug fix
Depends on: none directly, but required for #54's AC3 and #58's reset tests

Reported problem

Acceptance criterion 3 ("updating any profile section resets the decay penalty") keys off photographers.updated_at. Most profile sections live in child tables (portfolio, services, equipment, availability, sublocations), and writing them was assumed to never touch the parent row — 16 write-path call sites all call RecomputeAndSaveRanking afterward, but none of them write updated_at directly.

What investigation actually found

DirectoryPhotographer.UpdatedAt (*time.Time, field name UpdatedAt) is GORM's convention-recognized auto-update-time field (gorm/schema/field.go: any field literally named UpdatedAt with a Time data type gets AutoUpdateTime set with no explicit tag needed). RecomputeAndSaveRanking's existing config.GetConnPhotographers().Model(&p).Update("ranking", ranking) call already triggers that auto-bump on every invocation — confirmed empirically against GORM v1.31.1 by inspecting the exact SQL it emits via a sqlmock-backed probe: UPDATE photographersSETranking=?,updated_at=? WHERE id = ?.

So the real bug was the opposite of the one reported: updated_at was already being bumped on every RecomputeAndSaveRanking call — including from inside BackfillRanking's loop over the entire table (src/action/v1/photographers/maintenance.go). Every backfill run was silently wiping the freshness penalty for every photographer, not just leaving it unset for the 16 child-table write paths.

Fix (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go, maintenance.go)

Single choke point, not 16 call-site patches — every write path already funnels through RecomputeAndSaveRanking:

  • RecomputeAndSaveRanking(gothruUserId uint64) — unchanged public signature and behavior for the 14+ write-path callers. Internally calls recomputeAndSaveRanking(gothruUserId, preserveTimestamp=false), which uses GORM's .Update("ranking", ranking) — still bumps updated_at.
  • RecomputeAndSaveRankingPreserveTimestamp(gothruUserId uint64) — new. Calls recomputeAndSaveRanking(gothruUserId, preserveTimestamp=true), which uses .UpdateColumn("ranking", ranking) — UpdateColumn sets GORM's SkipHooks, which skips the auto-timestamp bump entirely.
  • BackfillRanking (maintenance.go) now calls RecomputeAndSaveRankingPreserveTimestamp instead of RecomputeAndSaveRanking.

Verification

  • Confirmed via actual emitted SQL (not just by reading the call site), per the issue's own explicit caveat that GORM's auto-timestamp behavior needed empirical confirmation.
  • TestRecomputeAndSaveRanking_BumpsUpdatedAt (computeRanking_ac3_test.go) — asserts the write-path SQL includes updated_at=?.
  • TestRecomputeAndSaveRankingPreserveTimestamp_DoesNotBumpUpdatedAt — asserts the backfill-path SQL omits updated_at entirely.
  • Checked all other references to photographers.updated_at in the codebase — none use it with a different meaning (no cache keys, sync jobs, exports, or SEO lastModified depending on it).
  • go build ./..., go vet ./... clean.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17

Acceptance criterion 3 — "updating any profile section resets the decay penalty" — cannot pass today, independent of any penalty work.

The bug

The penalty keys off photographers.updated_at. But most "profile sections" live in child tables, and writing them never touches the parent row.

Example — src/action/v1/portfolio/createPhotographerPortfolio.go:108 inserts into directory_portfolio and then only recomputes ranking:

if err := config.GetConnPhotographers().Create(&portfolioItem).Error; err != nil {
    return models.DirectoryPortfolio{}, err
}
invalidateRedisCache(&photographer, identifier)
go photographers.RecomputeAndSaveRanking(photographer.GothruUserID)

photographers.updated_at is untouched. Same shape in:

  • src/action/v1/services/addPhotographerServices.go:92 / removePhotographerServices.go:71
  • src/action/v1/photographers/addPhotographerEquipment.go:102 / removePhotographerEquipment.go:71
  • src/action/v1/availabilities/addPhotographerAvailability.go:88 / removePhotographerAvailability.go:67
  • src/action/v1/sublocations/addSublocation.go:111 / updateSublocation.go:94 / removeSublocation.go:56
  • src/action/v1/portfolio/createPhotographerPortfolio.go:115 / updatePhotographerPortfolio.go:123 / deletePhotographerPortfolio.go:71

So a photographer could add portfolio items, services and equipment every week and still be treated as stale. Only updatePhotographerProfile.go:302 and updatePhotographerLocation.go:80 write the parent row.

Fix

Do not patch 16 call sites. All of them already call RecomputeAndSaveRanking, so one write there covers every path:

src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go:135 currently does:

if err := config.GetConnPhotographers().Model(&p).Update("ranking", ranking).Error; err == nil {

Extend that update to also set updated_at. Single place, all callers fixed.

Watch out for

  • BackfillRanking calls the same function (src/action/v1/photographers/maintenance.go:105) in a loop over every photographer. If RecomputeAndSaveRanking starts bumping updated_at, running the backfill would mark every profile as freshly updated and wipe the penalty across the whole table. Needs a flag, a separate code path, or an explicit updated_at preservation in the backfill.
  • Confirm nothing else reads photographers.updated_at with a different meaning (cache keys, sync jobs, exports, SEO lastModified).
  • GORM may already auto-manage UpdatedAt on Model(&p).Update(...) — verify actual emitted SQL rather than assuming either way.

Done when

  • Any write to any profile section moves photographers.updated_at.
  • BackfillRanking does not move updated_at.
  • Confirmed via SQL, not just by reading the code.

issues.display_title: Issue #56: Ranking freshness: index check for updated_at on the v2 search path
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #56 — Index Check for updated_at on the v2 Search Path

Status: Partial — code-level analysis complete, EXPLAIN blocked on live DB access
Type: Performance investigation
Depends on: #54

Scope

After #54, both ORDER BY and the keyset WHERE in /v2/photographers/users use a computed expression involving updated_at:

GREATEST(ranking - CASE WHEN (updated_at IS NULL OR updated_at < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 365 DAY)) THEN 20 ELSE 0 END, 0)

The task: check existing indexes, EXPLAIN the query before/after, and confirm whether the expression forces a filesort at production row counts.

What was confirmed from the repo

  • No migration files exist anywhere in this repository (searched for any *migration* path — none found). Schema and indexes are managed outside this codebase.
  • DirectoryPhotographer (src/models/directory_photographer.go) has no index gorm tags on any field — only unique on gothru_user_id, slug, email. Neither ranking nor updated_at is declared indexed from the Go side, consistent with #52's finding that the pre-existing ORDER BY ranking DESC, rating_avg DESC, id DESC was already an unindexed filesort.
  • The post-#54 expression is a computed CASE/GREATEST expression, which no ordinary single-column index can serve directly — regardless of whether updated_at itself is indexed.

Blocked

This development environment has no reachable database — .env is absent (only .env.example with blank credentials), and there is no production-scale dataset available to test against. Running EXPLAIN or producing a real query plan without a live connection would mean fabricating numbers, which was avoided.

What's needed to close this out

Someone with access to DB_PHOTOGRAPHERS_* (staging or a production replica) needs to run:

EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM photographers
WHERE status IN (3,4)
ORDER BY GREATEST(ranking - CASE WHEN (updated_at IS NULL OR updated_at < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 365 DAY)) THEN 20 ELSE 0 END, 0) DESC,
         rating_avg DESC, id DESC
LIMIT 20;

— both with and without the continentId/countryId/cityId joins from getPhotographers.go, at real row counts.

Recommendation if it does degrade

Because the expression can't be indexed as-is, the fix isn't a simple composite index — it would mean reopening #52 toward option B/C (a persisted, indexable column), which is exactly the tradeoff #52 already weighed and rejected for the cost of a migration + cron. Recommendation: ship #54 as shipped, measure with the query above, and only reopen #52 if the filesort is actually shown to matter at current row counts. Per #52's own note, latency on this query is more likely dominated by other factors — the dead cross-DB fetch (fixed in #59), cross-DB IN lists, and three Preloads.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17
Depends on: #54

The penalty puts updated_at into the ORDER BY and the keyset WHERE of the hottest query in the service.

Scope

  • Check the existing indexes on the photographers table — is updated_at indexed at all? Is there a composite covering (ranking, rating_avg, id) that the current keyset pagination relies on?
  • EXPLAIN the v2 search query before and after the change (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go), with filters applied (search, continentId, countryId, cityId) and without.
  • A CASE WHEN updated_at < ... expression in ORDER BY is generally not index-usable and can force a filesort over the whole result set. Confirm whether that actually happens at production row counts.
  • If it degrades: consider a composite index, or reconsider option B (generated column) from #52.

Done when

  • EXPLAIN output for the v2 search, before and after, attached as a comment.
  • Either no regression, or an index added that removes it.

issues.display_title: Issue #57: Ranking freshness: Redis cache serves pre-decay ordering past the 1-year boundary
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #57 — Redis Cache Serves Pre-Decay Ordering Past the 1-Year Boundary

Status: Done — measured and accepted, no code change
Type: Investigation / decision
Depends on: #54

Problem

Every existing cache invalidation for the v2 photographer list is write-triggered: RecomputeAndSaveRanking clears PhotographerListV2Pattern() on save. The freshness penalty has no write event — it flips purely because the clock passed 365 days — so a cached list page can keep serving pre-decay ordering indefinitely after a profile crosses the boundary, unless the cache naturally expires.

Findings

  • The PhotographerListV2 cache key TTL is a flat 24 hours (helpers.RedisCacheTTL = 60 * 60 * 24, src/helpers/redis_keys.go).
  • Confirmed ordering is baked in: GetPhotographers (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go) serializes and caches the entire response map, including the ordered photographers array, keyed per (search, filters, cursor, size, cacheVersion) combination. So the stale-ordering window for any given cached page equals the TTL exactly, as predicted.
  • Confirmed every existing invalidation path is write-triggered — there is no independent expiry mechanism tied to the freshness boundary itself.

Decision: accepted, not reduced

The issue's own scope treats a short (minutes/hours) TTL as "bounded and acceptable — document it and close." 24 hours is within that bucket:

  • It's an existing, already-bounded TTL, not unbounded or absent — worst case is a once-per-cache-entry, up-to-24h-old view of one page slice, not permanent staleness.
  • Every cache key naturally re-populates with fresh ordering on its next miss regardless of writes — the drift self-corrects without manual intervention.
  • Adding a daily flush or shortening the TTL would trade a bounded, already-acceptable staleness window for either new scheduled-job infrastructure or more cache misses (and more DB load) on every page — for a decay effect that only matters on the exact day a given profile crosses the 1-year threshold. Not justified (YAGNI).

Outcome

No code change. Maximum staleness window: 24 hours, accepted explicitly and documented here and in the issue thread.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17
Depends on: #54

Problem

Every existing cache invalidation is triggered by a write. RecomputeAndSaveRanking clears the list cache on save (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go:136):

_, _ = helpers.ClearRedisKeys(helpers.RedisKey.PhotographerListV2Pattern())

The freshness penalty has no write event — it flips purely because the clock passed 365 days. So a cached v2 list page can keep serving pre-decay ordering indefinitely after a profile crosses the boundary.

This is the same class of problem as #52, one layer up: time-dependent output behind a write-invalidated cache.

Scope

  • Find the TTL on PhotographerListV2Pattern keys. If it is short (minutes/hours), the drift is bounded and acceptable — document it and close.
  • If the TTL is long or absent, add a bounded expiry or a daily flush of the list cache.
  • Check whether getPhotographers v2 caches full serialized pages (ordering baked in) or just row data. If ordering is baked in, the stale-ordering window equals the TTL exactly.

Done when

  • The maximum window during which a decayed profile can still be served at its old rank is measured and written down.
  • That window is either accepted explicitly or reduced.

issues.display_title: Issue #58: Ranking freshness: tests for decay, boundary, reset and pagination stability
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #58 — Tests for Decay, Boundary, Reset, and Pagination Stability

Status: Done — shipped in PR #60
Type: Test coverage
Depends on: #54, #55

Approach

All tests run against sqlmock (already used elsewhere in this repo — github.com/DATA-DOG/go-sqlmock) — no live database required. Exact SQL text for every mocked query was captured empirically (via a throwaway probe exploiting sqlmock's mismatch error, which prints the actual query GORM emits) rather than guessed, so the mocks reflect real GORM v1.31.1 output.

Freshness penalty (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers_test.go)

Tests effectiveRanking directly, which mirrors the SQL expression used in production:

  • TestEffectiveRanking_FreshProfile_Unchanged — updated yesterday, across all tier baselines (0/20/40/60/79): score unchanged. Regression guard on existing behavior.
  • TestEffectiveRanking_StaleProfile_Penalised — 400 days stale: base - 20.
  • TestEffectiveRanking_StaleProfile_ClampsAtZero — low base minus penalty: clamps at 0, never negative.
  • TestEffectiveRanking_ExactlyOneYear_NotYetPenalised — exactly 365 days: fresh side of the boundary (<, not <=), asserted explicitly per #53.
  • TestEffectiveRanking_OneYearAndOneDay_Penalised — 366 days: penalised, confirming the boundary sits exactly where intended.
  • TestEffectiveRanking_NullUpdatedAt_TreatedAsStale — nil updated_at: penalised, no panic.

effectiveRanking takes an injected now time.Time specifically so the exact-boundary case is deterministic instead of racing the wall clock between test setup and the function call under test.

AC3 reset (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking_ac3_test.go, needs #55)

  • TestRecomputeAndSaveRanking_BumpsUpdatedAt — asserts the emitted SQL is UPDATE photographers SET ranking=?,updated_at=? ... (write paths reset the penalty).
  • TestRecomputeAndSaveRankingPreserveTimestamp_DoesNotBumpUpdatedAt — asserts UPDATE photographers SET ranking=? ... with no updated_at (what BackfillRanking now calls) — regression guard against the "backfill wipes every penalty" bug discovered while implementing #55.

A single test per code path was sufficient instead of one case per profile section: all 16 write-path callers funnel through the same RecomputeAndSaveRanking/recomputeAndSaveRanking function, so testing that one function covers every section, consistent with #55's single-choke-point fix.

v2 pagination (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers_pagination_test.go, needs #54)

TestGetPhotographersV2_PagesAcrossFreshnessBoundary — seeds 3 photographers straddling the boundary (2 fresh, 1 stale) at page size 2, pages through the full set, and asserts:

  • Every photographer appears exactly once across both pages (rankings [60, 50] then [40] — no gaps or duplicates).
  • Ordering is monotonically non-increasing by effective ranking.
  • hasMore/nextCursor bookkeeping is correct on both pages.
  • The emitted SQL text (via ExpectQuery regexes) requires the literal GREATEST(ranking - CASE ... expression to appear in both the keyset WHERE and the ORDER BY — so reverting the ORDER BY back to raw ranking would fail this test.

Honest limit of this test

sqlmock never executes SQL — it can prove the Go code assembles the correct query text and correctly threads returned rows through the pagination bookkeeping (cursor effective score, response mapping, hasMore/nextCursor), but it cannot prove the SQL is semantically correct against a real MySQL engine (e.g. that GREATEST/CASE/DATE_SUB behave as expected). That would require an embedded MySQL instance or testcontainer, judged not worth the infrastructure cost for this change — the test comment states this limitation explicitly rather than overclaiming coverage.

Verification

go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./... all clean across the whole repository.

Parent: GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17
Depends on: #54, #55

Extend the existing src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking_test.go and add v2 search coverage.

Cases

Freshness penalty

  • Profile updated yesterday → score unchanged from current behaviour (regression guard on all existing tiers).
  • Profile updated 400 days ago → penalised by the agreed amount from #53.
  • Profile updated exactly 365 days ago → assert which side of the boundary it lands on. < vs <= is the kind of off-by-one that ships silently.
  • updated_at is NULL (the column is *time.Time, src/models/directory_photographer.go:21) → decide and assert: treat as stale, or treat as fresh? Must not panic.

AC3 reset (needs #55)

  • Stale profile → write each profile section in turn (profile, location, service, availability, equipment, sublocation, portfolio) → assert updated_at moved and the penalty is gone. One case per section; this is exactly where the current bug hides.
  • BackfillRanking over a table of stale profiles → assert updated_at did not move and penalties survive.

v2 pagination (needs #54)

  • Seed a set that straddles the penalty boundary, page through it fully at a small page size, assert every photographer appears exactly once and ordering is monotonic. This is the regression test for the keyset cursor.

Done when

  • All cases pass.
  • The boundary case and the NULL updated_at case are asserted explicitly, not left implicit.

issues.display_title: Issue #59: v2 photographer list: dead cross-DB user fetch on every non-search request + ~100 lines of dead tier code
issues.main_description_html:
Issue #59 — v2 Photographer List: Dead Cross-DB User Fetch + Dead Tier Code

Status: Done — shipped in PR #60
Type: Bug fix / cleanup (unrelated to the ranking-freshness feature, filed separately)
Depends on: none — recommended to land before #54, since it touches the same function

Problem 1: wasted full-table cross-DB read on every non-search request

In GetPhotographers (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go), the non-search branch fetched every GothruUser with subscribtion IN (1,2,5,6,7,8) from a second database connection (GetConnGothruMod) and then never read the result — the loop that built searchUserIds only appended when isSearch, and the WHERE gothru_user_id IN filter on the main query only applied when isSearch. The non-search branch is the default path (plain directory browse, homepage), so this fired on every request that missed the Redis cache.

Fix: moved the GothruUser fetch entirely inside if isSearch. Non-search requests no longer touch GetConnGothruMod() at all.

Problem 2: was the subscription filter meant to be applied?

The discarded else branch specifically selected subscribed tiers (1,2,5,6,7,8) — the same values tierBaseline treats as paid. Two possibilities needed resolving: the filter was obsolete (safe to delete), or it was supposed to be applied and free-tier photographers were leaking into the directory (a correctness bug).

Resolution: traced git history. Commit 287ec61 ("fix(v2): replace tier-based sort with ranking-based cursor pagination") deliberately removed the old tier-partitioned pagination scheme and its own commit message states: "Search filter (searchUserIds) preserved unchanged." Only the search-path fetch was meant to survive that refactor — the non-search subscribtion IN (...) fetch was leftover from the old scheme, never re-wired to filter anything after that commit. Confirmed dead, not a correctness bug: no subscription filtering was intended to apply to the plain directory/homepage browse path post-refactor. Recorded as a comment on #59 per the issue's own requirement, so it doesn't resurface as an open question later.

Problem 3: ~100 lines of dead tier-pagination code

getGreaterTierCondition, getSameTierCondition, and their only caller-of contains had no callers anywhere in the repository — leftovers from the tier-partitioned pagination scheme replaced by commit 287ec61's ranking-based keyset cursor. Deleted (~100 lines), making the remaining pagination logic (which #54 needed to modify) noticeably shorter and easier to reason about.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./... clean.
  • No behavior change: the non-search branch already applied no effective subscription filter before this change (the fetched users were never read in that branch); status IN (3,4) on DirectoryPhotographer is untouched; search-branch logic untouched.
  • Done ahead of #54 as recommended in the issue — the keyset cursor logic in this file was ~100 lines shorter before #54 touched it.

Found while scoping GoThruMedia/gothru-photographer-v2#17. Unrelated to that feature — filing separately.

This is the hottest read path in the service: getPhotographersV2 backs the directory page and the homepage in gothru-photographer-v2 (src/components/directory-page.tsx:166,189,228, src/app/page.tsx:86).

1. Every non-search request does a wasted full-table read across DB connections

src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go:169-211:

isSearch := search != ""
var users []models.GothruUser

if isSearch {
    err := config.GetConnGothruMod().Model(&models.GothruUser{}).
        Where("first_name LIKE ? OR last_name LIKE ?", "%"+search+"%", "%"+search+"%").
        Find(&users).Error
    // ...
} else {
    err := config.GetConnGothruMod().Model(&models.GothruUser{}).
        Where("subscribtion IN ?", []int{1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8}).
        Find(&users).Error          // <-- line 193
    // ...
}

var searchUserIds []int
for _, u := range users {
    if isSearch {                   // <-- only populated when isSearch
        searchUserIds = append(searchUserIds, u.UserID)
    }
}

query := config.GetConnPhotographers().Model(&models.DirectoryPhotographer{}).
    Where("status IN ?", []int{3, 4})

if isSearch {
    query = query.Where("gothru_user_id IN ?", searchUserIds)   // <-- only used when isSearch
}

In the non-search branch, every GothruUser with subscribtion IN (1,2,5,6,7,8) is hydrated into memory from a second database connection (GetConnGothruMod), and then nothing reads it. The loop only appends when isSearch; the WHERE only applies when isSearch.

The non-search branch is the default path — plain directory browse and homepage. So this fires on every request that misses the Redis cache.

Fix: move the fetch inside the if isSearch branch. It is already there for the search case; the else branch just needs to be deleted.

2. Open question: was the subscription filter meant to be applied?

The else branch specifically selects subscribed tiers (1,2,5,6,7,8) — the same values tierBaseline treats as paid (src/action/v1/photographers/computeRanking.go:28-35). Someone wrote that filter deliberately, but its result is discarded, so the v2 list currently applies no subscription filter at all — only status IN (3,4).

Two possibilities, and they need different fixes:

  • The filter is obsolete → the fetch is simply dead, delete it (fix 1 above).
  • The filter was supposed to be applied → free-tier photographers are currently leaking into the directory listing, which is a correctness bug, and the fix is to apply it (ideally as a join or a persisted tier column, not an in-memory IN list).

Needs a decision before deleting. Check git history on this file for when the else branch stopped being used.

3. ~100 lines of dead tier-pagination code

getGreaterTierCondition (src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go:47-98) and getSameTierCondition (:100-138) have no callers anywhere in the repo. contains (:38-45) is used only by those two, so it dies with them.

They take subs58, subs16, subs27, premiumUserIds — leftovers from a tier-partitioned pagination scheme that the current ranking-based keyset cursor replaced. Deleting them removes roughly a quarter of the file and makes the remaining pagination logic readable, which matters because #54 has to modify exactly that logic.

Scope

  • Move the user fetch into the isSearch branch (pending the answer to §2).
  • Resolve §2 explicitly — record the answer in a comment either way.
  • Delete getGreaterTierCondition, getSameTierCondition, contains.
  • Confirm no behaviour change to the v2 response: same photographers, same order, same pagination.

Ordering vs #54

Worth doing before #54. That task edits the keyset cursor in this same function, and it is easier to reason about once the dead code is gone.

Done when

  • Non-search requests issue no query against GetConnGothruMod.
  • §2 answered in a comment.
  • Dead functions removed, go build and existing tests pass.
  • v2 list output verified unchanged.
